hints.title: Duplicate Permutation Obstacle
hints.text: When the input array contains duplicate values, standard permutation trees explore identical candidate leaves multiple times. How can ordering candidates prevent duplicate permutations without auxiliary sets?

hints.title: Preceding Sibling Usage Invariant
hints.text: Sort nums. Only allow using nums[i] if its identical duplicate nums[i-1] is already used in the current branch, skipping when nums[i] == nums[i-1] and not used[i-1].

hints.title: Used-Array Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Sort nums. Maintain a boolean array used of length n. When picking an element at position i: if used[i] is true, continue. If i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1] and not used[i-1], skip i. Mark used[i] = true, recurse, then reset used[i] = false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of elements in nums (1 <= N <= 8)
complexity.notes: Bounded by N! unique permutations with duplicate pruning at each tree level.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all permutations and deduplicating in a set wastes factorial time on redundant paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The boolean used array requires O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using the not used[i - 1] condition to enforce canonical order among duplicates.
